questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you ride?

options.text: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the car's driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle helmet do to protect you best?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible damage.

questions.question: Can a car and a motorcycle share a lane?
questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles both need a full lane width to operate safely. Lane sharing is not allowed.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
Other drivers may need the lane.
It is hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to a vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not know you are there. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What benefit do motorcycle gloves provide?

options.text: They make it hard to control the motorcycle and should not be worn.
They help other drivers see you.
They help you grip the handlebars better.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you grip the handlebars better.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Even though a motorcycle is narrower than a car:

options.text: It still needs a full lane width to operate safely.
It can share a lane with a car for short distances.
It must share a lane with a car in heavy traffic.
It can ride on the shoulder when traffic is crowded.

questions.correctAnswerText: It still needs a full lane width to operate safely.
questions.explanation: Despite their small size, motorcycles need a full lane width to operate safely. Lane sharing is not allowed.

questions.question: How does carrying a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It makes no difference in handling.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It changes how the motorcycle handles.
It should be done by beginning riders to gain experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a traffic lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars form a slippery strip in the center of lanes. In dry conditions, motorcycles can usually operate safely on this strip.

questions.question: What kind of pants should a motorcycle rider wear?

options.text: Loose enough to flap in the wind.
Short pants that expose your legs.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they restrict your movement.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black text. These signs tell you the traffic rules. You must follow them.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. You need to know what is behind you. Mirror checks should be part of your regular driving routine.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before you ride your motorcycle. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual tells you about your specific bike.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than most other vehicles.
Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
Should not be used if no vehicles are close to the motorcycle.
Are more complicated than those on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals every time you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do. Use them even if you think no one is nearby. Signals help keep you safe.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should be especially cautious of:

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.

questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. A car may pull out into the street or leave its parking space without warning.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them go ahead. Do not ride faster. This can make the danger worse.
